The boundary is Flask’s `request` `LocalProxy` over `_cv_request`; Flask binds that `ContextVar` during `RequestContext.push()`. Werkzeug 2.0+ stores locals in `ContextVar`s, so visibility follows Python context propagation rather than thread-local state.

Relevant files:

- [sg-evals/flask--2.3.3:src/flask/globals.py?L55-L72](/r/github.com/sg-evals/flask--2.3.3/-/blob/src/flask/globals.py?L55-L72) - Defines `_cv_request` and exposes `request = LocalProxy(_cv_request, "request", unbound_message=...)`.
- [sg-evals/flask--2.3.3:src/flask/ctx.py?L231-L265](/r/github.com/sg-evals/flask--2.3.3/-/blob/src/flask/ctx.py?L231-L265) - `AppContext.push()` binds `_cv_app`; `pop()` resets it.
- [sg-evals/flask--2.3.3:src/flask/ctx.py?L280-L346](/r/github.com/sg-evals/flask--2.3.3/-/blob/src/flask/ctx.py?L280-L346) - `RequestContext` owns the request object and context tokens.
- [sg-evals/flask--2.3.3:src/flask/ctx.py?L358-L385](/r/github.com/sg-evals/flask--2.3.3/-/blob/src/flask/ctx.py?L358-L385) - `RequestContext.push()` ensures an app context, then executes `_cv_request.set(self)`, making Flask’s request proxy available.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:src/werkzeug/local.py?L40-L50](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/src/werkzeug/local.py?L40-L50) - Documents `Local`’s switch to `ContextVar` storage in Werkzeug 2.0.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:src/werkzeug/local.py?L104-L143](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/src/werkzeug/local.py?L104-L143) - `LocalStack` is backed by a `ContextVar`; `push()` reads with `.get()`, copies, and sets the stack.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:src/werkzeug/local.py?L467-L521](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/src/werkzeug/local.py?L467-L521) - `LocalProxy` builds `_get_current_object`; for a `ContextVar`, it calls `local.get()`, converts `LookupError` into `RuntimeError`, then resolves the requested attribute.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:CHANGES.rst?L690-L696](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/CHANGES.rst?L690-L696) - Records the `Local` transition from `threading.local` to `ContextVar`.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:docs/local.rst?L11-L23](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/docs/local.rst?L11-L23) - Explains that context locals are scoped to threads, asyncio tasks, or greenlets, and that `ContextVar` replaced thread-local storage.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:docs/local.rst?L29-L43](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/docs/local.rst?L29-L43) - Shows the `ContextVar` → `LocalProxy` pattern and states that an unset variable raises `RuntimeError`.
- [sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7:tests/test_local.py?L121-L133](/r/github.com/sg-evals/werkzeug--2.3.7/-/blob/tests/test_local.py?L121-L133) - Asyncio test demonstrating task-local stack copies with `ensure_future`.
- [sg-evals/flask--2.3.3:docs/async-await.rst?L42-L73](/r/github.com/sg-evals/flask--2.3.3/-/blob/docs/async-await.rst?L42-L73) - Flask’s async-view execution model and warning that spawned tasks may be cancelled under WSGI.

Chain: Flask request handling pushes `RequestContext` → `_cv_request.set(self)` → `request` proxy invokes `ContextVar.get()` → missing task context raises Flask’s “Working outside of request context.” A normal `asyncio.create_task(coro)` captures the currently running task’s context (equivalent to using a copied context), so the child generally sees the request context. A coroutine scheduled from a thread-pool worker has that worker thread’s current context instead; if it has no copied request context, `ensure_future(coro)` cannot recover the parent task’s context, and Werkzeug’s `ContextVar.get()` reaches the unbound `LocalProxy` path, producing the Flask runtime error.
